d: Post-processing effects are customizable filters that quickly enrich the visuals of a game.
h:
Post-processing effects are customizable filters that allow you to quickly enrich the visuals of your game. Using the post-processing effect objects in the Lighting service or Camera, you can:

  • Simulate a camera viewing a bright light and exaggerate its glow (bloom).
  • Apply a Gaussian blur to the entirety of your game, or add a blur to parts of your game that aren't in focus (depth‑of‑field).
  • Enhance an environment's appearance to create a specific mood through hue (color correction).
  • Render a halo of light that moves with the sun (sun rays).

Add post-processing effects

When you add post-processing effects to the Lighting service, they display to all players who enter the game. This is useful for effects that affect the global environment, such as sun rays.

When you add post-processing effects to the Camera object, they only display to a specific player. This is useful for effects that should only pertain to that player based on their actions, such as blurring the 3D world view when they have a UI menu open.

To add post-processing effects to either the Lighting service or Camera:

  1. In the Explorer window, hover over the Lighting service or Camera, then click the ⊕ button. A contextual menu displays.

  2. From the menu, insert one or more of the following post-processing effects:

  3. BloomEffect

  4. BlurEffect
  5. ColorCorrectionEffect
  6. DepthOfFieldEffect
  7. SunRaysEffect

  8. ColorGradingEffect

  9. Depending on your Studio settings, some effects may not appear. To increase your rendering quality level:

  10. Open Studio Settings.

  11. In the left-side navigation, select Rendering, then the Editor Quality Level dropdown menu.
  12. Set it to the highest level.

Bloom

The BloomEffect effect exaggerates lights within your game by simulating a camera viewing a bright light. When this effect has a high value, parts with light colors glow.

Blur

The BlurEffect effect applies a Gaussian blur to the entirety of the 3D world view. You can use this effect to blur the background when a player has a menu open, allowing them to focus on the most important details.

Color correction

The ColorCorrectionEffect effect adjusts color properties to enhance an environment's appearance. You can also use this effect to provide player feedback, such as tinting the screen red when their character's health is low.

The following list describes the primary ColorCorrectionEffect properties:

  • Brightness — Sets the brightness of pixels.
  • Contrast — Sets the change in separation between dark and light colors.
  • Saturation — Sets the intensity of colors.
  • TintColor — Determines how much the RGB channels of pixels scale.

Depth-of-field

The DepthOfFieldEffect effect blurs parts of your game that aren't in focus. You can use this effect to blur distant objects or to focus a player on specific parts of your game, such as an item in a shop.

Sun rays

The SunRaysEffect effect creates a halo of light with rays around the sun that move based on the ClockTime or TimeOfDay property. Objects between the player's camera and the sun shape this effect, allowing for realistic visuals of light and shadow.

Color grading

The ColorGradingEffect effect modifies how color values calculated by the renderer should be converted to the screen's color range, impacting the mood and appearance of your place.

This effect's primary property is TonemapperPreset. The following values are available:

  • TonemapperPreset.Default — Sets the tone mapper to use the post‑2019 Roblox appearance which provides vivid colors and high contrasts.
  • TonemapperPreset.Retro — Sets the tone mapper to imitate the pre‑2019 Roblox appearance. Colors look less saturated and there's less contrast between them.

If you wish to recreate a full pre‑2019 Roblox look for your game, experiment with TonemapperPreset.Retro and set the brightness of all lights to a maximum of 1.0.

kid.simple: Post-processing effects are filters applied to the whole picture on screen, like filters on a photo app. They can make bright things glow, blur the world, change colors and mood, or add sun rays. Put them in `Lighting` and every player sees them. Put them in the player's `Camera` and only that one player sees them, which is great for things like a red screen when health is low.
kid.analogy: Post-processing is like putting colored glass or a soft-focus lens in front of a camera. The scene itself does not change; only how it looks through the lens does.
keyPoints: Effects inside `Lighting` show for all players. Effects inside the `Camera` show only for one player.
To add one in Studio: hover over Lighting or Camera in the Explorer, click the plus button, and pick an effect.
If an effect does not appear, raise Editor Quality Level in Studio Settings, under Rendering.
`BlurEffect` blurs the whole 3D view, like when a menu is open. `DepthOfFieldEffect` blurs only things out of focus.
`ColorCorrectionEffect` changes `Brightness`, `Contrast`, `Saturation`, and `TintColor`, for example tinting the screen red at low health.
`SunRaysEffect` adds rays of light around the sun that move with the time of day.
`ColorGradingEffect` with `TonemapperPreset` set to `Retro` gives a pre-2019 Roblox look; `Default` gives vivid, high-contrast colors.

terms.post-processing: Changing the final picture after the 3D scene is drawn, like editing a photo after you take it.
terms.filter: An effect laid over the whole screen that changes how everything looks.
terms.Camera: The object that decides what each player sees. Each player has their own camera.
terms.bloom: A glow around bright lights, like squinting at a lamp.
terms.Gaussian blur: A smooth, even blur over the whole view.
terms.depth of field: Keeping one distance sharp while closer or farther things are blurry, like a phone's portrait mode.
terms.contrast: How different darks and lights are. High contrast makes darks darker and brights brighter.
terms.saturation: How strong colors are. 0 change is normal; lower looks washed out; higher looks extra colorful.
terms.tint: A color laid over the screen. A red tint makes everything look reddish.
terms.tone mapper: The step that turns the game's light values into colors your screen can show.
terms.rendering quality: How detailed the graphics are. Some effects only show at higher quality.

example.title: Red screen when health is low
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local camera = Workspace.CurrentCamera

-- This effect is in the Camera, so only this player sees it
local lowHealthTint = Instance.new("ColorCorrectionEffect")
lowHealthTint.TintColor = Color3.fromRGB(255, 120, 120)
lowHealthTint.Saturation = -0.3
lowHealthTint.Enabled = false
lowHealthTint.Parent = camera

local function onCharacterAdded(character)
	local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
	lowHealthTint.Enabled = false
	humanoid.HealthChanged:Connect(function(health)
		-- Turn the tint on below 30 percent health
		lowHealthTint.Enabled = health < humanoid.MaxHealth * 0.3
	end)
end

if player.Character then
	onCharacterAdded(player.Character)
end
player.CharacterAdded:Connect(onCharacterAdded)
explain: The LocalScript creates a `ColorCorrectionEffect` and puts it in this player's camera.
`TintColor` makes the screen reddish and the negative `Saturation` makes colors a bit duller.
It starts turned off with `Enabled = false`.
Whenever health changes, the tint turns on if health is under 30 percent of max health, and off otherwise.
It reconnects each time the character respawns.

watchOut: Putting a personal effect like a menu blur in Lighting. Everyone would see it; use the player's Camera.
Thinking an effect is broken in Studio. Check that Editor Quality Level is set high.
Overdoing bloom or blur. Too much makes the game hard to see; use small values.
